newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hes Beheer to cut 280 jobs at EBS unit.
newsitem.headline: Hes Beheer to cut 280 jobs at EBS unit.

text.p: Transport and storage group Hes Beheer said on Tuesday it planned to shed 280 jobs at its European Bulk Services unit to safeguard EBS's future in the face of a structural decline in bulk cargo volumes.

Hes said it had drawn up a plan in consultation with management consultants McKinsey to ensure the long-term continuity of EBS as a going concern even with a structural decline in the bulk volumes handled.
"The plan is based on a work force of 371. This means that 280 jobs need to be shed as quickly as possible," the company said in a statement.

It said EBS needed to concentrate and modernise its activities and drastically slim down. Under the plan, activities will be concentrated at the Laurenshaven and Europoort terminals, with more use being made of contract labour.
The Vulcaanhaven and Botlek terminals would be given over to different uses, it said.
Hes said that in the years ahead it would invest in upgrading bulk handling equipment and terminals, the capacity of which would be reduced by around a third.

It said unions and the port employers' association had been invited to discuss the job losses at a meeting tomorrow. Under a 1993 port accord, unions and employers have an obligation to seek a solution for job losses.
